title: Escalation Paths & Ownership Map (Escalation Playbook v2)
author: Owen Phillips
content:
h1. Purpose
This page defines *who owns what* across Redwood Inference (Hosted, Dedicated, Private) and *how Support routes and escalates* issues. It is designed to:

* Reduce ping-pong between teams by making component boundaries explicit.
* Protect paging hygiene by clarifying when to page vs when to file an engineering ticket.
* Standardize the “first stop” owner for common customer-reported symptoms (5xx, timeouts, streaming disconnects, 429s, Dedicated capacity issues, Private SSO/networking/audit log issues).

h1. Guiding principles
* *Route by component + blast radius, not by customer loudness.*
* *Support owns customer-facing triage and comms.* Engineering/SRE owns mitigation and technical resolution.
* *Page only when the issue meets paging criteria* (see “Paging rules”), otherwise use async escalation.
* *Private / enterprise customer details may be restricted.* When in doubt, restrict artifacts and use approved channels.

h1. Quick routing decision tree (Support)
1) *Identify deployment mode*
   * Hosted API (shared multitenant)
   * Dedicated (reserved capacity pool)
   * Private (customer VPC/on-prem)

2) *Classify symptom*
   * Availability errors: 5xx, elevated error rate
   * Performance: timeouts, p95/p99 latency spikes
   * Streaming: disconnects / broken streams
   * Throttling: 429s / quota / rate limit
   * Auth: login failures, invalid tokens, SSO/SAML (Private)
   * Networking: Private connectivity, DNS, egress/ingress, TLS
   * Data/security: suspected exposure, audit logs not delivered

3) *Check Known Issues first*
   * If there is a validated workaround: apply + document confirmation.
   * If known issue does not match: proceed to escalation.

4) *Decide escalation mode*
   * If Sev0/Sev1 or paging criteria met: *page oncall* (SRE or Security) and open an incident if required.
   * Otherwise: create engineering ticket + tag owner team; request logs/metadata; provide SLA-appropriate updates.

h1. Ownership map (components → primary team)
The table below is the default ownership mapping. If a customer is blocked and ownership is ambiguous, escalate to *SRE oncall* to coordinate.

h2. Service/component ownership table
|| Area || What it includes (examples) || Primary owner || Secondary / consult || Support routing notes ||
| API Gateway / Edge | Request termination, routing entrypoint, TLS, request-id generation, header normalization, streaming proxy behavior at edge (when applicable). (Services: *redwood-edge*, *api-gateway*) | *SRE (Edge)* | Runtime (for stream semantics), Security (for WAF/abuse) | If symptoms are *region-wide*, *multi-customer*, or show *5xx before model selection*, start with SRE. Provide request IDs + region + time window. |
| Auth & RBAC (Hosted/Dedicated) | API keys, org/project auth, role checks, token issuance/validation. (Services: *auth-service*, *rbac-service*) | *Security Engineering* | SRE (availability), Support Eng (misconfig triage) | If customers see *401/403* and it is not explained by misconfiguration, route to Security Eng. For widespread auth failures, page SRE and loop Security. |
| Quota / Rate limit / 429 enforcement | Quota configs, rate limit buckets, burst policies, org/project limit enforcement. (Services: *quota-service*, *rate-limit*) | *API Gateway & Rate-limit SME (Platform)* | SRE (capacity), Support Eng | Most 429s are misconfig/usage-pattern issues. If 429 rate spikes suddenly for many orgs or differs from configured limits, escalate to Platform + SRE. |
| Scheduler / Router / Batching | Smart routing, model selection, continuous batching controller, queueing, admission control. (Services: *inference-router*, *batcher*) | *Routing & Orchestration (Hosted/Dedicated)* | Runtime, SRE | If timeouts correlate with *queue depth* or *admission control*, route here. Attach router logs link + request IDs. |
| Serving runtime (GPU inference) | Model server, kernel selection, KV cache, streaming token generation, runtime OOMs, CUDA errors, performance regressions by model/version. (Services: *serving-runtime*, *model-server*) | *Runtime Engineering* | SRE (infra), Research/Applied ML (model onboarding) | If errors occur *after* model selection or are model-specific (e.g., only one pinned version), route to Runtime Eng. |
| Model catalog / registry | Model availability, pinned versions, rollout/canary config, model metadata, deprecations. (Services: *model-registry*, *catalog*) | *Runtime Engineering* | Product (external comms), SRE (availability) | If a pinned model version fails or is missing, route to Runtime Eng. Ensure customer request includes model + version + region. |
| Observability & logging pipeline | Metrics/tracing ingestion, dashboards, log retention, runbook links. | *SRE (Observability standards)* | Support Eng | If a customer issue is unresolved due to missing telemetry, route to SRE Observability for instrumentation gaps; do not page unless it blocks incident response. |
| Dedicated capacity control plane | Dedicated pools, autoscaling policies, capacity reservations, noisy-neighbor isolation, routing policies for Dedicated. (Services: *dedicated-orchestrator*, *capacity-manager*) | *SRE (Dedicated oncall)* | Routing & Orchestration, Runtime | Dedicated latency spikes/capacity shortfalls: start with SRE Dedicated oncall. Include pool ID, region, expected QPS, and dashboards link. |
| Private deployments (installer + upgrades) | Installer, Helm charts, upgrade paths, customer-managed config, VPC integration. (Artifacts: *private-installer*, *charts*, *airgap bundle*) | *Private Deployments* | SRE (reliability), Security (hardening) | For Private: route to Private Deployments first unless it is a *security incident* or *platform outage* impacting many tenants. |
| Private SSO/SAML | SAML/OIDC integration, IdP configs, certificate rotation, login redirect loops. | *Security Engineering* | Private Deployments | For Private SSO failures: Security owns auth correctness; Private Deployments owns config/installer integration. Route to Security first if errors appear in auth logs; otherwise Private Deployments for config validation. |
| Audit logs / compliance exports | Audit event generation, delivery to customer sinks, retention guarantees (Private). | *Security Engineering* | Private Deployments | If audit logs stop flowing for a regulated customer, treat as high priority. Determine whether it is delivery/config vs generation bug. Restrict customer identifiers in shared channels. |
| SDKs (Python/TS/etc.) | Retry/backoff defaults, streaming client implementation, timeout guidance, error mapping. | *DevEx / SDK Engineering* | Support Eng, Docs | If issue is client-side retry/stream parsing, route to SDK Eng. If it causes widespread impact, coordinate with SRE. |

h1. Paging rules (protecting oncall)
Support should page oncall only when the situation meets the criteria below. Otherwise, use async escalation (ticket + Slack thread) and follow the SLA update cadence.

h2. Page SRE oncall when ANY of the following are true
* *Sev0/Sev1 impact* per the Severity Matrix (e.g., widespread outage, major regional degradation, critical customer production down with no workaround).
* *Multi-customer impact* is confirmed or strongly suspected (e.g., multiple orgs reporting 5xx/timeouts in the same region/model).
* *Active incident indicators* are present (status page triggers, automated alerts, sustained elevated error rate).
* *Dedicated capacity shortfall* causing sustained timeouts/failed requests for a Dedicated customer during contracted usage.
* *You need an immediate mitigation* (failover, rollback, traffic shift) that only SRE can execute.

h2. Do NOT page SRE oncall for
* Single-customer integration questions (SDK usage, prompt formatting, expected 429 behavior).
* Known issue with validated workaround that resolves the customer within SLA.
* Low-volume, transient errors without evidence of sustained impact.
* “Please take a look” escalations without required metadata (see required fields below).

h2. Page Security oncall immediately when ANY of the following are true
* Suspected *data exposure*, cross-tenant data leak, credential compromise.
* Confirmed or suspected *unauthorized access* to a customer’s account/project.
* Private enterprise incident involving regulated data where the customer asserts a compliance breach.

For Security paging: treat all details as *restricted*; avoid posting customer identifiers outside approved channels.

h1. Escalation channels and mechanisms
h2. Standard channels
* #support (triage coordination)
* #eng-oncall (engineering oncall coordination; do not post sensitive customer info)
* #incidents (incident coordination; use incident-bot)
* #security-incident (security incidents; restricted handling)
* #eng-sre (SRE async questions)
* #docs (doc/KB updates)

h2. Systems of record
* Customer ticket: Jira *SUP-* (customer-facing support record)
* Internal process/tooling: Jira *INT-* (Support ops)
* Engineering work: Linear *ENG-* (bugfixes, runbooks, tooling)
* Incident record: incident tooling (created via incident-bot) + postmortem/RCA doc where required

h2. incident-bot usage (when paging)
When paging SRE/Security, start with incident-bot “Support Escalation” so required context is captured consistently.

h1. Required information for any engineering/SRE escalation
Support must provide these fields before requesting action (paging or async).

* Customer org/project (or anonymized ID if restricted)
* Deployment mode: Hosted / Dedicated / Private
* Region(s)
* Model + version (or “latest”) and endpoint type (chat/completions/embeddings/rerank)
* Request IDs (minimum 3) and timestamps with timezone
* Exact error codes/messages (include HTTP status; for streaming specify client library)
* Impact statement: user-visible symptoms + approximate request volume affected
* What changed recently (customer-side and Redwood-side if known): model pinning, rollout, SDK upgrade, network/IdP changes
* Links: dashboards/traces (if available), log extracts (sanitized), and the SUP ticket key

If any of the above are missing, the first action is *data collection*, not paging.

h1. Common symptoms → default escalation path
|| Symptom customers report || Likely component || First route (async) || Page? || Notes / fast checks ||
| Elevated 5xx across many requests | API Gateway / Edge OR Runtime | SRE (Edge) + Runtime (if model-specific) | Yes if sustained >10 min or multi-customer | Check region, status page, compare across models. Gather request IDs and whether failures happen pre/post model selection. |
| Timeouts (non-streaming) | Router/Batching OR Dedicated capacity | Routing (Hosted) or SRE (Dedicated) | Page if Sev1 or customer production down without workaround | Check queue depth, admission control, pool saturation, customer timeout settings. |
| Streaming disconnects | Edge streaming proxy OR Runtime | SRE (Edge) + Runtime | Page if widespread or critical enterprise workflow impacted | Confirm client read timeouts, reconnect logic, and whether disconnects correlate with region/model. Use streaming known-issue checklist. |
| 429 throttling | Quota/Rate-limit OR customer burst | Platform (quota/rate-limit) | Page only if sudden multi-customer spike or mismatch with configured limits | Verify org/project limits, burst settings, and proper exponential backoff in client. |
| Dedicated p99 latency spikes during peak | Dedicated control plane + capacity manager | SRE (Dedicated) | Page if violating Dedicated SLA / sustained | Check pool utilization, noisy-neighbor indicators, autoscaling events, routing policy drift. |
| Private SSO/SAML login failures | Security (SSO) + Private Deployments | Security Eng (SSO) | Page Security if suspected compromise or widespread outage | Collect IdP metadata change timeline, cert rotation, error screenshots/logs. Restrict account identifiers. |
| Private networking/connectivity issues | Private Deployments | Private Deployments | Page only if platform-wide regression across multiple Private installs | Validate DNS, TLS, firewall rules, cluster health, recent upgrades. |
| Audit logs not delivered (Private) | Security (audit pipeline) OR config | Security Eng | Page Security if compliance risk + no workaround | Determine whether event generation or sink delivery is failing; gather sink config + timestamps. |

h1. Handoff boundaries (what each team is responsible for)
h2. Support / CS
* Owns initial triage, information capture, and customer communication cadence.
* Applies validated Known Issues workarounds.
* Initiates escalation and ensures the escalation packet is complete.

h2. SRE
* Owns incident coordination for availability/performance issues in hosted infrastructure.
* Owns traffic shifts, rollbacks, regional mitigations, and alerting/runbook updates.
* Owns Dedicated capacity mitigation and operational controls.

h2. Runtime Engineering
* Owns model-serving correctness and runtime behavior (including streaming generation behavior beyond the edge proxy).
* Owns model/version rollbacks and serving runtime bug fixes.

h2. Security Engineering
* Owns authentication, authorization, security incidents, and audit log correctness.
* Owns investigation and customer/security comms alignment for sensitive incidents.

h2. Private Deployments
* Owns Private installer/upgrade mechanics and customer-environment integration.
* Coordinates with Security and SRE as needed for Private incidents.

h1. Backup and escalation-of-escalation
If the primary owner does not respond within the engagement SLA for the ticket’s severity/tier:
1) Re-post in the original escalation thread with the SLA timestamp and missing action.
2) Escalate to the functional lead:
   * SRE: *Rafael Mendes* (oncall) / *Sean Gallagher* (lead)
   * Runtime: *Mateo Alvarez* / *Noah Patel*
   * Security: *Marcus Lin* / *Fiona McCarthy* (incident coordination)
   * Private: *Vivek Kulkarni*
3) If still blocked and customer impact is increasing, page SRE oncall to coordinate ownership.

h1. Change management
This ownership map is updated during the Escalation Playbook v2 rollout and reviewed quarterly with Support + SRE.
